entries.claim: Radiohead drew on Charles Mingus's jazz for 'Pyramid Song'.

sources.title: Prog: Radiohead’s proggiest moments
sources.evidence: The Pyramid Song section identifies Mingus as its musical source.

sources.title: The Irish Times: Taking music to strange places
sources.evidence: In a Colin Greenwood interview, the song is described as based on Mingus.

entries.claim: On 'Teachers', Daft Punk named Chicago house musicians among their influences.

sources.title: DJ Mag: Homework at 25 — Teachers and Students
sources.evidence: Describes Teachers as homage to house originators, with sections on Chicago producers.

sources.title: Rolling Stone: Paul Johnson, Celebrated Chicago House Producer, Dead at 50
sources.evidence: Identifies Chicago producer Johnson as an influence acknowledged by name in Teachers.

entries.claim: James Brown's funk was an influence on Kraftwerk.

sources.title: Electronic Beats: A week in the life — 168 hrs Kraftwerk, NYC, part 1
sources.evidence: Juan Atkins recalls Florian Schneider telling him about the James Brown influence.

sources.title: Croatian Encyclopedia: Kraftwerk
sources.evidence: National encyclopedia names James Brown and funk among the group’s early influences.

entries.claim: Red Hot Chili Peppers recorded a cover of Stevie Wonder's 'Higher Ground'.

sources.title: Rolling Stone: Red Hot Chili Peppers on 25 Years of Mother’s Milk
sources.evidence: Chad Smith describes the band recording the Stevie Wonder cover.

sources.title: Guitar World: Flea’s bittersweet hip-hop recording experience
sources.evidence: Opening paragraph independently identifies the 1989 Higher Ground release as a Wonder cover.

entries.claim: The White Stripes covered Son House's 'Death Letter'.

sources.title: Rolling Stone: The White Stripes Share 2000 Performance of Death Letter
sources.evidence: Identifies the recorded 2000 performance as a Son House cover.

sources.title: The Guardian: The White Stripes bring the blues back to rock
sources.evidence: Performance corroboration.

entries.claim: Arctic Monkeys recorded Barbara Lewis's 'Baby I'm Yours' with the 747s.

sources.title: NME: Arctic Monkeys covers revealed
sources.evidence: Reports the Barbara Lewis cover and collaboration with the 747s.

sources.title: Complete Music Update: Arctic Monkeys collaborate with 747s on next single
sources.evidence: Oisin Leech tells CMU how Turner invited the group to record the Lewis cover.

entries.claim: Coldplay used the riff from Kraftwerk's 'Computer Love' in 'Talk'.

sources.title: NPO Radio 2: Coldplay leent de basis voor Talk van Kraftwerk
sources.evidence: Explains that Coldplay transferred the Computer Love synthesizer riff to guitar.

sources.title: LA Weekly / Arthur: A conversation with Ralf Hutter of Kraftwerk
sources.evidence: Jay Babcock’s 2005 interview introduction identifies the borrowed Computer Love riff.

entries.claim: Nina Simone's version of 'Wild Is the Wind' inspired David Bowie to record it for Station to Station.

sources.title: NPO Radio 2: David Bowies Wild Is The Wind is een eerbetoon aan Nina Simone
sources.evidence: Describes Bowie’s recording as a response and tribute to Simone’s rendition.

sources.title: Verve / UMe: Nina Simone’s Historic Philips Years Celebrated with Vinyl Remasters
sources.evidence: Record-label release explicitly identifies Simone’s rendition as the inspiration for Bowie’s album recording.

entries.claim: Talking Heads drew on Fela Kuti's Afrobeat when making Remain in Light.

sources.title: Library of Congress: Remain in Light — Talking Heads
sources.evidence: Kevin Buck describes the album’s instrumental sessions as based on Fela-pioneered Afrobeat rhythms.

sources.title: Pitchfork: Talking Heads — Remain in Light
sources.evidence: Dan Brooks identifies Fela’s Afrodisiac as Eno’s model for the album.

entries.claim: Paul Simon recorded 'Mother and Child Reunion' in Jamaica with musicians who had backed Jimmy Cliff.

sources.title: Jamaica Observer: Simon’s reggae classics get new life
sources.evidence: Reports the Jamaican recording with Cliff’s backing musicians, naming Jackson, Grennan and Hinds.

sources.title: NPO Radio 2: Mother & Child Reunion — Paul Simon
sources.evidence: Public broadcaster confirms the Jamaica session with Jimmy Cliff’s regular musicians.

entries.claim: Peter Gabriel made 'Sledgehammer' as a tribute to the soul music of Otis Redding.

sources.title: Peter Gabriel: Sledgehammer
sources.evidence: Gabriel describes the song as homage and identifies Redding as his favourite singer.

sources.title: Sound On Sound: Peter Gabriel — Behind The Mask (January 1987)
sources.evidence: Contemporary interview discusses the Redding tribute and participation of Redding’s trumpeter Wayne Jackson.

entries.claim: Massive Attack sampled Billy Cobham's 'Stratus' in 'Safe from Harm'.

sources.title: Hit Channel: Interview — Billy Cobham
sources.evidence: Cobham confirms licensing the Stratus sample in response to a question naming Safe from Harm.

sources.title: Rolf Großmann: Xtended Sampling 1995–2026, in Un_Making Beats, p. 97
sources.evidence: Academic discussion identifies the sampled accompaniment from Cobham’s Stratus and its jazz-fusion context.
